Day 01 · New YorkArrival and Midtown

AirTrain to Jamaica, then the LIRR to Penn — around 50 minutes and immune to traffic. A taxi is a flat fare to Manhattan but can take twice as long at that hour.

Land at JFK

AirTrain to Jamaica, then the LIRR to Penn — around 50 minutes and immune to traffic. A taxi is a flat fare to Manhattan but can take twice as long at that hour.

18:30Evening
Midtown on foot

Deliberately empty. Eat near the hotel and walk one neighbourhood; the jet lag is worse than you think.

Day 02 · DowntownThe harbour and the memorial

One ferry from Battery Park serves both islands and the ticket includes them. Take the first sailing — by ten the security queue runs long.

08:30Early
Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island

One ferry from Battery Park serves both islands and the ticket includes them. Take the first sailing — by ten the security queue runs long. Pedestal and crown access sell out months ahead.

Statue City Cruises ↑
13:00Afternoon
9/11 Memorial, then One World Observatory

The pools are free and open air; the museum below is ticketed and needs two hours. The observatory is a separate timed ticket, best in the last slot before sunset.

9/11 Memorial ↑
17:30Evening
Brooklyn Bridge on foot

Walk it from the Brooklyn side so Manhattan is in front of you the whole way. The pedestrian deck is now separated from the bike lane, which has made it bearable again.

Day 03 · UptownThe Met, the park, a curtain

Go straight to the American Wing. Hassam’s Winter in Union Square — the painting behind this page — hangs there, with Cole’s Oxbow and Bierstadt’s Lander’s Peak. Three hours minimum.

10:00Morning
The Metropolitan Museum of Art

Go straight to the American Wing. Hassam’s Winter in Union Square — the painting behind this page — hangs there, with Cole’s Oxbow and Bierstadt’s Lander’s Peak. Three hours minimum.

The Met ↑
14:00Afternoon
Central Park, south through the Ramble

The museum’s back door opens onto the park. Cut southwest to Bethesda Terrace and out at 59th — about an hour at a walking pace.

19:30Evening
One Broadway show

Book four to eight weeks out for anything current. Same-day TKTS discounts what has not sold, which is rarely the show you wanted.

TKTS ↑
Day 04 · TransitNew York to Las Vegas

About 5h45 westbound, and you gain three hours — a 09:00 departure lands near midday with the whole afternoon intact.

JFK → LAS, nonstop

About 5h45 westbound, and you gain three hours — a 09:00 departure lands near midday with the whole afternoon intact.

12:45Afternoon
Into the Strip

Harry Reid sits four miles from the Strip — roughly fifteen minutes by taxi, which is unusual for a major US airport. Check in and shower before the heat drops.

20:00Evening
Bellagio fountains, then the Strip on foot

Fountains run every half hour from afternoon, every fifteen minutes after eight. Free, and the best thing in the city that costs nothing.

Day 05 · Grand CanyonThe canyon, all day

Grand Canyon West is about 2h15 by road; the South Rim is closer to 4h30 and worth it only with a driver and the whole day. Book two to three weeks out.

Depart for the West Rim

Grand Canyon West ↑
11:00Midday
Skywalk, Eagle Point, Guano Point

The Skywalk is a separate ticket from park entry and cameras are not allowed on it — lockers at the entrance. Guano Point has the better view and no queue.

20:00Evening
Back on the Strip by eight

A long day. Eat near the hotel rather than booking anything that needs a reservation time you might miss.

Day 06 · Red RockSandstone, then a show

Twenty minutes west of the Strip; a 13-mile one-way loop with pull-offs. Timed entry is required October through May and sells out.

08:00Morning
Red Rock Canyon scenic loop

14:00Afternoon
Hoover Dam, or the pool

The dam is 45 minutes the other direction and pairs badly with Red Rock in one day. Offered as the alternative for anyone who would rather not spend the afternoon by the water.

20:30Evening
One show — Sphere or a residency

Book before you leave home. Sphere seats in the 200 level are the sweet spot; the front rows sit too close to read the screen.

Day 07 · The crossingLas Vegas to Toronto

Visa-exempt travellers flying into Canada need an electronic travel authorisation, applied for online. Most approvals are immediate; some take days.

—Before you fly
The eTA has to already exist

Visa-exempt travellers flying into Canada need an electronic travel authorisation, applied for online. Most approvals are immediate; some take days. An airline can refuse boarding without it, and there is no fixing it at the gate.

Canada eTA ↑
12:20Midday
LAS → YYZ, nonstop

About 4h15, and you give the three hours back. This is the border, and the only one on the trip — Canadian entry is at Pearson, not in the air.

17:00Afternoon
UP Express to Union

Twenty-five minutes from Pearson Terminal 1 to Union Station, every fifteen minutes, and it does not sit in traffic on the 427.

Day 08 · NiagaraThe falls, from the good side

About 1h30 each way down the QEW. The Canadian side faces the Horseshoe head-on, which is why Church painted from here and why the American side is the lesser view.

08:30Morning
Drive or coach to Niagara Falls, Ontario

About 1h30 each way down the QEW. The Canadian side faces the Horseshoe head-on, which is why Church painted from here and why the American side is the lesser view.

12:00Midday
Niagara City Cruises and Table Rock

The boat runs roughly April to November and stops once the river ices. Ponchos are provided and inadequate. Table Rock puts you at the lip of the Horseshoe for nothing.

Niagara City Cruises ↑
15:30Afternoon
Niagara-on-the-Lake on the way back

Twenty minutes north through the wine country. Worth the detour in September and October; skip it if the falls ran long.

Timed tickets; the earliest slot has the shortest queue and the clearest air. The glass floor is one level below the main deck and easy to miss.

St. Lawrence Market, then the Distillery District

The market is closed Mondays. The Distillery is a fifteen-minute walk east — Victorian industrial brick, pedestrian only.

Toronto Islands ferry

Fifteen minutes from Jack Layton Terminal to Centre Island. Go for the skyline looking back, not the island itself. Check the last return before you sail.

Where you sleep

Two candidates a city · nothing booked

Six shortlisted hotels, two per city, with the trade-offs kept rather than smoothed over. No ratings are quoted because none have been verified.

New York

JFK · New York · Nights 1–3
Bowery · Lower East Side citizenM Bowery

For

  • The best price per night in Manhattan for a room that is genuinely new
  • Downtown base puts the harbour and the 9/11 Memorial on your doorstep

Against

  • Rooms are small even by New York standards — a wall-to-wall bed and little else
  • Forty minutes to the Met on the 6 train, so Day 06 starts with a commute
Midtown · West 40s The Gallivant Times Square

For

  • Walk to every Broadway house — no train home after a late curtain
  • Central for the Met, Top of the Rock and Grand Central alike

Against

  • Times Square outside the door, at all hours, in all weathers
  • Rooms are dated next to the downtown options at a similar rate

Las Vegas

LAS · Nevada · Nights 4–6
Centre Strip · Las Vegas Blvd The Cosmopolitan

For

  • Terrace suites have real balconies over the Bellagio fountains — rare on the Strip
  • Walkable to Bellagio, Aria and the Sphere without a taxi

Against

  • Resort fee on top of the nightly rate, charged at checkout
  • Every route to your room crosses the casino floor
CityCenter · non-gaming Vdara

For

  • No casino and no smoking indoors — the quietest sleep on the Strip
  • All suites have kitchenettes; a bridge connects straight to Bellagio

Against

  • No casino also means none of the noise people come to Vegas for
  • Resort fee still applies; restaurants are next door, not downstairs

Toronto

YYZ · Ontario · Nights 7–9
Front Street · opposite Union Station Fairmont Royal York

For

  • The UP Express from Pearson terminates across the road — no transfer with bags
  • Ten minutes on foot to the CN Tower, the ferry docks and St. Lawrence Market

Against

  • Very large and often full of a conference; the lobby is never quiet
  • Standard rooms in the older wing are small for the rate
Exhibition Place · waterfront Hotel X Toronto

For

  • Lake and skyline views that no downtown hotel can offer
  • Rooftop pool and a genuinely quiet night

Against

  • No subway station within walking distance — a streetcar or a taxi every time
  • Adds twenty minutes to each end of the Niagara day

The route

Three cities

Pick one

New York

Three nights · JFK · subway and feet
Arrive
JFK → Manhattan

AirTrain to Jamaica, then the LIRR to Penn Station. About 50 minutes and immune to traffic. A yellow cab is a flat fare to Manhattan but can take 90 minutes at the wrong hour.

~50 min
Getting about
OMNY, tapped straight in

No card to buy — tap a contactless card or phone at the turnstile and the fare caps itself after twelve rides in a week. The subway runs all night, which no other city on this trip does.

All week
Day 02
Hotel → Battery Park

4 or 5 train to Bowling Green, then five minutes on foot to the ferry queue. Go before nine or the queue eats the morning.

~25 min
Day 02
Battery → 9/11 Memorial

Ten minutes on foot up Greenwich. No transit needed; the whole of the Financial District is walkable.

~10 min walk
Day 02
Brooklyn Bridge, east to west

Walk it from the Brooklyn side. High St station on the A/C puts you at the ramp; you come off at City Hall.

~35 min walk
Day 03
Hotel → The Met

The 6 train to 86th Street, then four blocks west through the park edge. From downtown allow 35 minutes.

~35 min
Day 03
The Met → Midtown

Walk out of the museum’s back door into Central Park, cut southwest through the Ramble to Bethesda Terrace, and leave at 59th. An hour at a walking pace, and the best hour of the day.

~60 min walk
Depart
Manhattan → JFK

Reverse the LIRR. Leave three hours before a domestic departure; the AirTrain adds fifteen minutes on top of the train.

~50 min

Las Vegas

Three nights · LAS · the Strip is longer than it looks
Arrive
LAS → the Strip

Harry Reid sits four miles from the Strip — about fifteen minutes by taxi and roughly $25. There is no train, and the rideshare pickup is a long walk from baggage claim.

~15 min
Getting about
Distances lie here

Bellagio to the Venetian looks like three blocks and takes twenty-five minutes on foot, most of it indoors through casinos. Budget double whatever the map says, and use the Deuce bus or a rideshare after dark.

All week
Day 05
Strip → Grand Canyon West

Coach or small-group pickup from the Strip hotels, about 2h15 each way on US-93. Pickups start before dawn; the South Rim is 4h30 and needs its own day.

~2h15 each way
Day 06
Strip → Red Rock Canyon

Twenty minutes west on Charleston Boulevard. A rental car for the day is the simplest way; the scenic loop is one-way and 13 miles.

~20 min
Day 06
Alternative — Hoover Dam

Forty-five minutes southeast on US-93. It pairs badly with Red Rock on the same day, so treat it as the other option, not an addition.

~45 min
Depart
Strip → LAS

Fifteen minutes, but the security queue at Harry Reid runs long on Sunday afternoons. Two and a half hours for a domestic flight.

~15 min

Toronto

Three nights · YYZ · UP Express, TTC and the QEW
Arrive
YYZ → Union Station

The UP Express from Terminal 1, every fifteen minutes, twenty-five minutes end to end, and it does not sit in traffic on the 427. Buy on the platform or in the app.

~25 min
Getting about
PRESTO, or tap to pay

The TTC takes contactless straight at the gate. Lines 1 and 2 cover everything downtown, and the 501 and 504 streetcars fill the gaps. Downtown itself is walkable end to end.

All week
Day 08
Toronto → Niagara Falls

About 1h30 each way down the QEW by car or coach. The Canadian side faces the Horseshoe head-on, which is why you are on this side of the river.

~1h30 each way
Day 08
Detour — Niagara-on-the-Lake

Twenty minutes north through the wine country on the way back. Worth it in September and October; skip it if the falls ran long.

~20 min
Day 09
Union → CN Tower

Ten minutes on foot from Union through the SkyWalk, indoors the whole way, which matters in February.

~10 min walk
Day 09
St. Lawrence Market → Distillery

Fifteen minutes east on foot, or the 504 streetcar if the weather has turned. The market is closed Mondays.

~15 min walk
Day 09
Jack Layton Terminal → Centre Island

A fifteen-minute sail from the foot of Bay Street. Check the last return before you go; winter service is thin.

~15 min sail
Depart
Union → YYZ

UP Express again. If you fly home through the United States you clear US customs at Pearson before boarding, so add an hour on top.

~25 min + 1h

Paperwork, plainly

Two countries, one trip
ESTA

United States authorisation under the Visa Waiver Program, for the Vegas and New York legs. Apply well before departure — approval is not instant and an airline can refuse boarding without it.

United States · valid 2 years
eTA

Canada's electronic travel authorisation, needed for the flight into Toronto. Applied for online; usually approved in minutes, occasionally in days.

Canada · valid 5 years
I-94

Your US arrival record and the only place your permitted stay is written down. Read the admit-until date on arrival — it is not always the date you assumed, and leaving for Canada mid-trip does not reset it.

Issued at entry
Preclearance

Toronto Pearson clears US customs before you board, not after you land. It only matters if you fly home through the United States — and then it needs an extra hour at YYZ.

Departure day only

Requirements change. Every itinerary ships with a link to the official source for each item, re-checked the week you travel.
